message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the maximum speed you may drive.
• On highways, 55–75 mph is common; on rural roads, 55 mph.
• Speed limits can be lower in construction zones, school zones, or where posted. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• School buses stopping to pick up or drop off children must be stopped. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights are only for foggy conditions. | | **Parking** | • No parking on the left side of a curb in a residential area.
• Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited unless marked.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles that are abandoned or unsafe may be towed.
• The towing company must notify the owner and the police. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Proof of insurance is required; minimum liability coverage is $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 for property damage. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Minor infractions (e.g., speeding 1–20 mph over the limit) may result in a fine and points on your driving record.
• Major infractions (e.g., reckless driving, DUI) can lead to higher fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Special Zones** | • School zones: Speed limit is 25 mph during school hours.
• Construction zones: Speed limits may be reduced to 20–35 mph.
• Residential zones: Speed limits are often 35 mph. | ### How to Stay Informed 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Offers up‑to‑date traffic regulations and road safety tips. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. 3. **Local County Websites** – Some counties have additional ordinances (e.g., parking restrictions). ### Quick Tips - Always obey posted signs; they are the law. - Keep your vehicle’s registration and insurance documents in the car. - If you’re unsure about a specific rule, check TxDOT’s website or consult a local attorney. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular law or scenario!
